subject: classics
intro: Classics leads to the work of interpreting, teaching and preserving the ancient world — museums and archives, scholarship and publishing, and the classrooms where Greece and Rome are still taught.

roles.title: Historians
roles.what: Research and interpret the past: gather and weigh primary sources, build accounts of how societies and institutions worked, and publish books, articles and reports for archives, museums, publishers and government.
roles.where: Unit 8's Athenian institutions, critics of democracy and empire-ideology topics, and unit 2's Augustan Rome material, train the source-based argument this career is built on.

roles.title: History Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach history at universities: lecture on periods and themes, lead seminar discussion of sources, grade and supervise student writing, and carry a research agenda in your own specialism.
roles.where: The syllabus's Homer-to-reception sequence — epic, theatre, art, religion, democracy — is precisely the classical-civilisation content such teachers put into university courses.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Preserve historically valuable records: appraise documents and papers, catalogue them, safeguard fragile originals, and help scholars and the public retrieve the material evidence of earlier times.
roles.where: Unit 9's reception theory and the classical-curriculum debate give the contextual judgement archives of antiquarian material demand, alongside the close-reading habits of the epic units.

roles.title: Curators
roles.what: Care for and present museum collections: acquire and authenticate objects, plan exhibitions, write interpretation, manage loans and budgets, and make ancient material legible to modern visitors.
roles.where: Units 4 and 5 — Parthenon sculpture, vase painting, Roman portraiture and propaganda, Pompeii — are the art-historical grounding curators of classical collections use daily.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Create original written work: draft and revise books, scripts, articles and other pieces, work with editors and publishers through revisions, and shape material for the audiences a publisher or client needs reached.
roles.where: Unit 1's epic technique and oral tradition, unit 3's tragedy and comedy, and unit 9's antiquity-in-film reception supply the plots, archetypes and allusions writers mine from antiquity.
